Example Grid orders four small modular reactors

Example Grid ordered four small modular reactors from Northwind Atomics on Tuesday, in a deal the utility valued at 4.2 billion dollars. The first unit is expected to reach the site in 2029, with commissioning slipping to 2031.

Regulators in Ontario have not yet approved the design, and the utility said it would not begin site preparation until they do. A decision is expected within eighteen months, according to two people familiar with the filing.

The order is the largest placed by a Canadian utility since 1994. Northwind said the reactors would deliver 1200 megawatts in total, enough to replace two retiring gas plants on the same interconnection. The company declined to say whether further orders were planned, and would not comment on financing.

Analysts noted that the schedule assumes regulatory approval arrives on time, which has not been the pattern for the technology anywhere it has been attempted. Example Grid said it had built contingency into the delivery window and that the contract carries penalties for late delivery on both sides.

The utility serves roughly 3.4 million customers across the province and has committed to retiring its remaining fossil generation by 2035. It has not said how much of that replacement capacity the reactors are expected to supply.
